analysis: Reviewed CI-only changes in .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml (head lines 533-1539) and .github/workflows/register-model.yml (runner change at head line 95-96). No provider runtime, coordinator protocol, attestation, key-handling or cache code is touched, so the threat model assets (A-001..A-020) and the TB-002/TB-003/TB-007/TB-011 boundaries are not affected by these diffs. provider-tests.yml: adds a cluster_gpu input and a non-blocking test-cluster-gpu job. The build jobs now run only when inputs.cluster or inputs.provider is 'true', so a push whose tree was already tested skips builds. The gate job still requires the expected job results. Third-party actions remain pinned to SHAs. Restored .git caches are validated before use (no symlinks, hooks, fsmonitor, hooksPath or includes). Checkouts use persist-credentials false, and ci-plan-checks and provider-test-gate have contents:read. The new tested-tree record uploads (lines 1514-1539) contain only tree and base/head names and component flags, with no secrets. Artifacts are retained for 14-30 days. The GPU lane is opt-in via a label and non-blocking, so it does not weaken the gate for blocking tests, though the cluster-test-plan audit is still enforced. register-model.yml: runner changes from blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404 to GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 with a 30-minute timeout. The publishing key MODEL_REGISTRY_PUBLISHING_KEY is still only sent after the coordinator URL allowlist check, to the two Darkbloom coordinators. Moving to a GitHub-hosted ephemeral runner does not obviously weaken secret handling. Open integration questions (not findings): the trigger conditions and the tested-tree skip logic live in provider-plan.yml and scripts/ci-tested-tree.py, which were not supplied. Whether the skip-on-already-tested-tree path can bypass the required tests for a release-bound tree depends on them. No security regression is demonstrated here.
